cases.task: What free way can I use to file my taxes this year?
cases.toolOutput:
The free way that may fit you is Guided Free File.
Guided Free File asks simple questions, one at a time. The software does the math.
Last season it was free for people with income of $95,000 or less. Check IRS.gov for this year's limit.
Each company also sets its own rules, such as age or state. Some companies do your state return for free, some charge.
Free File was closed when we checked on November 4, 2026. The IRS says it opens in January 2027. Check IRS.gov.
Free help from a VITA volunteer: 800-906-9887.
Always start at IRS.gov/freefile: https://www.irs.gov/freefile
You type your Social Security number yourself on the free filing site you pick on IRS.gov.
Your answers so far. First name: Ana. Last name: Rivera. Street address: 12 Example Street. City: Springfield. State: IL. ZIP code: 62701. Birth date: 02/29/1960. Phone number: 555-010-1234. Papers ticked: 3 of 9.
Note: This is a list of answers, not a tax return. You make your account, sign, and press Submit yourself.
expect: says Guided Free File may fit
says to start at IRS.gov/freefile
says to check IRS.gov for this year's limit
says Free File was closed when checked on November 4, 2026 and opens in January 2027
says the person types their Social Security number on the free filing site you pick on IRS.gov
gives no advice about what to claim

cases.task: My income was over the limit and I do not want to do it all myself. What free choice do I have?
cases.toolOutput:

Free File Fillable Forms works at any income.
You type into online copies of the IRS forms. Only some of the math is done for you.
State taxes are not included.
If you would rather not do the work yourself, a VITA volunteer can help for free.
Free help from a VITA volunteer: 800-906-9887.

cases.task: I filled in my answers file but something looks wrong. Can you check it?
cases.toolOutput:
Fix this first: Are you filing this year's taxes? Use yes, no, or unsure.
Fix this first: First name: use letters only. No numbers.
Fix this first: State: pick your state from the list.
Fix this first: ZIP code: type 5 numbers, like 12345.
Fix this first: Birth date: pick a real date.
Fix this first: Phone number: type 10 numbers, like 555-010-1234.
Fix this first: Papers: one item is not on the list.
Note: Nothing was saved or sent. Fix the lines above and run it again.
expect: lists the problems to fix before moving on to anything else
says the first name must be letters only
says the ZIP code needs 5 numbers
says the birth date must be a real date
asks the person to fix the lines and try again
does not guess a value for any box

cases.task: I do not know my income number from last year. What do I do?
cases.toolOutput:
First, find your income number.
The IRS calls your income number adjusted gross income, or AGI.
You can see it by signing in to your IRS online account, under Tax Records.
You can also ask the IRS to mail you a copy of last year's return.
